summary: This House resolution sets floor procedures, including waived points of order, one hour of debate, and a motion to recommit, for considering two joint resolutions disapproving DOE energy conservation standards for walk-in coolers, freezers, and commercial refrigerators plus H.R. 1048 on foreign gift disclosures and contract bans for colleges.

scores.thoughts: The resolution sets procedural rules for considering two Congressional Review Act disapprovals of DOE energy efficiency rules and one bill on foreign contracts in higher education. None of these measures involve appropriations, budget authority, or direct changes to government spending levels.
No provisions in the underlying measures or the procedural resolution address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue policy.
The bills concern energy standards and foreign influence in higher education; there is no connection to healthcare coverage, markets, or regulation.
No reference to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appears in the text.
The legislation does not address immigration pathways, border enforcement, or related protections.
No provisions relate to reproductive health services or abortion access.
Neither the energy-rule disapprovals nor the higher-education foreign-contracts bill affects military or defense budgets or policy.

Sections 1 and 2 of the resolution provide for House consideration of H.J. Res. 24 and H.J. Res. 75, which would disapprove DOE energy-conservation standards for commercial refrigeration equipment. These standards constitute environmental/energy-efficiency regulations; facilitating their repeal therefore limits such regulations.
No provisions touch welfare programs, food assistance, or related entitlements.

While H.R. 1048 amends the Higher Education Act, its focus is exclusively on foreign-gift disclosure and contract prohibitions; it does not address federal funding for public schools, school choice, or privatization.
No content relates to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance regulation.
The resolution and underlying measures contain nothing on sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
H.R. 1048 restricts certain foreign contracts by institutions of higher education, but this is framed as a national-security/foreign-influence measure rather than a trade or tariff policy.
No fiscal, deficit, or debt-ceiling provisions are present.
No language addresses legal protections or restrictions related to LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bills do not authorize, modify, or restrict foreign assistance programs.
No election-administration, voting-access, or campaign-finance provisions exist.
Nothing in the text concerns technology regulation, data privacy, or platform oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
The resolution and underlying bills do not engage religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
